reason: The cited evidence shows SLL structures improve thermal stability in Ge-Sb-Te phase-change materials by managing Sb precipitation, but the hypothesis applies this to a completely different Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-P alloy system without any evidence that such layering or the Sb-related mechanism is relevant. The key premise of transferability is entirely unsupported, and the mechanism is misrepresented as general when it is specific to Sb-rich chalcogenides.
premises: Superlattice-like (SLL) structures can enhance thermal stability in phase-change materials.
The mechanism involves modulation of physical/chemical properties and reduction of Sb-phase impact on stability.
SLL structures can balance phase-change speed and thermal stability.
The cited SLL evidence from Ge-Sb-Te systems is directly transferable to a Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-P high-entropy alloy.
